steps.label: Magnesium (Z = 12)
lines: Magnesium has atomic number 12, so it
The two outer electrons are both in the
steps.why: Filling in order of rising energy places two electrons in 1s, two in 2s, six in 2p and the last two in 3s, so magnesium ends with a filled outer s pair, which is the group 2 ending.
common_mistakes: Writing 3s¹ 3p¹ for the outer pair. Both outer electrons of magnesium are in the 3s orbital.
The shorthand [Ne] 3s² is correct chemistry, but this question asks for the complete form, so write every subshell out.
steps.memory_tip: Neon's ten electrons plus the 3s pair make magnesium's twelve.
steps.margin_note: Add the superscripts; they must total the atomic number.

steps.why: Calcium has eight electrons more than magnesium: six fill 3p and the last two enter 4s, which lies below 3d in energy, so calcium also ends in an outer s pair.
common_mistakes: Writing 3d² for the last two electrons. The 4s orbital is lower in energy than 3d, so 4s fills first.
Choosing an element outside group 2. The alkaline earth metals are beryllium, magnesium, calcium, strontium, barium and radium.
steps.memory_tip: Argon's eighteen electrons plus the 4s pair make calcium's twenty.
steps.margin_note: The question allows any two group 2 metals; write each with its atomic number.

insider_note: Pick the two easiest to count, magnesium and calcium, and check each by adding the superscripts to the atomic number.
